records.issue_text: [BUG] The .small-action block is redesigned (flexbox conversion, padding changed from '0.5em 0 0.5em 4em' to '0 1.5%', removal of margin-top, removal of p padding-top) even though the stated intent is header layout optimization, and the new padding breaks the 4em indent that aligned .small-action-desc with the avatar column. Small-action rows (deleted posts, closed notices, custom messages in topics) lose their avatar-column indentation and vertical spacing; this is a visual regression in topic streams with no traceable requirement in 'optimize header layout performance'.
records.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `.small-action` layout/styling: it adds flexbox/align-items and alters `.small-action-desc` from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%;` (and removes `> p { padding-top: 4px; }`, plus sets inner `p { margin: 0; }`). This removes the fixed 4em left indent that likely aligned the description with the avatar column, so the reported loss of indentation/spacing is a plausible visual regression introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] .panel is assigned @include order(3) while its flex siblings (.title, and .extra-info-wrapper which gets order(2) in topic.scss) are styled in two different files, creating hidden cross-file coupling with no order(1) ever defined. The next developer reordering or adding a header child must discover the scattered order values across header.scss and topic.scss to avoid mis-ordering; DOM-order-dependent rendering breaks silently when markup order changes because only two of the children carry explicit orders.
records.rationale: The diff introduces explicit flex ordering in multiple stylesheet files: `.panel` in `header.scss` now has `@include order(3)` (and `.contents` is made a flex container via `@include flexbox()`), while `topic.scss` adds `@include order(2)` to `.extra-info-wrapper`. In these changes, no other related elements are given explicit `order`, meaning other flex items will fall back to the default order, and understanding/adjusting the resulting visual order requires finding these scattered order values across files. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The align-items mixin passes $alignment verbatim into -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, but the 2009/2011 box specs expect different keywords (start/end instead of flex-start), so the prefixed lines are dead or invalid for the alignment values this diff actually uses beyond center. The badges.css.scss call with align-items(baseline) emits -ms-flex-align: baseline, which IE10 treats as invalid and falls back to flex-start, so legacy-browser users see mis-aligned category badges; the mixin silently promises cross-browser support it does not deliver.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Hand-maintained parallel vendor mixin set (flexbox/inline-flex/align-items/order each repeating five prefixed lines) duplicates what a library like Compass/Bourbon provides, and the `order` and `align-items` mixins have already drifted (order emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group` but align-items omits the matching `-moz-box-align`, and includes the invalid `-ms-align-items`), showing the copies are not consistently maintained. The next person adding a flex mixin (e.g. justify-content) copies the drifted pattern, and each browser prefix must be fixed in every mixin separately rather than one source of truth.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the '&.bullet { margin-top: 5px }' override on .badge-wrapper inside .extra-info-wrapper is an unexplained behavioral deletion that changes vertical alignment of bullet-style category badges, unrelated to the claimed performance goal. Forums configured with the bullet category style see category badges in the topic header sit 5px higher than the previous accepted layout, a silent visual drift outside the accepted intent of the PR.
records.rationale: The diff in `app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic.scss` removes a specific style override for bullet badges: inside `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper`, the nested `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` block is deleted. That is a concrete behavioral/layout change (vertical positioning) for `.badge-wrapper.bullet` within the topic header area, and the diff does not show any direct replacement adjustment in that same scope to preserve the previous offset.
